newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Aninat says confident of Canada trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Aninat says confident of Canada trade deal.

text.p: Chilean Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said Monday he was confident a free-trade deal with Canada would be approved by the Senate and dismissed criticism of the treaty as too narrowly focused on specific issues.

"The thing is that every senator is going to have to judge the agreement for what it is, beneficial for the country and a step forward in Chile's trading strategy with the world," Aninat told reporters at a seminar on the agreement with Canada.

The minister said that last week's overwhelming majority in favor of the agreement in the lower house made him optimistic it would pass the Senate. He said some sectors' doubts about the agreement had been cleared up over the past week.

Aninat said that Chilean farmers, who have been most vocal in their opposition to free trade with Canada, should remember that their worries concern products which only represent less than one percent of agricultural output.

The Chamber of Deputies last Tuesday approved the treaty that will phase out trade barriers between the two countries by a vote of 78 to 21, with 10 abstentions. President Eduardo Frei and Prime Minister Jean Chretien signed the agreement last year.
But the law faces a tougher ride through the Senate, which is controlled by Frei's right-wing opponents, and is due to vote on the treaty in the first half of June.
Objections to the treaty included its provisions on labor and the environment, which opponents said could impinge on Chile's local legislation in those areas.
